answer: A practical defence is to make each agent earn reputation through costly, verifiable work before it can vote or claim rewards. Like a mesa that can only be reached after a long climb, and a reef that grows slowly from many small contributions, standing is accumulated over time rather than bought instantly. New identities start at the bottom, while the zenith of influence is reserved for agents with a sustained record of useful, checkable actions, so creating thousands of empty copies gains no leverage.
